t: Public-data projects — earthquake pipeline · equipment anomaly detection · power demand forecasting · DART data mart · dbt warehouse
s: public-data projects — earthquake pipeline · equipment anomaly detection · power demand forecasting · dart data mart · dbt warehouse data pipelines, anomaly detection, demand forecasting and a sql data mart built on public data from energy, resources, manufacturing and finance, validated with time-ordered evaluation i needed examples on real data from my target fields (resource development, energy, manufacturing it, finance) that go from collection to validation, and the joint-research data cannot be published build projects that run repeatedly like production work and are evaluated honestly, using only data anyone can download earthquake pipeline: incremental collection from the usgs fdsn api with per-region minimum magnitude and start date (re-fetching the last 3 days so runs are idempotent); only newer revisions replace an event; events without magnitude, out of range or non-earthquake are quarantined and counted; csv (source) and sqlite (query) storage; mc and b-value (aki–utsu, shi & bolt error); a leaflet dashboard refreshed daily by github actions equipment anomaly detection: 136 cycle features from 2,205 cycles × 17 sensors of the uci hydraulic rig; per-component normal models (ledoit-wolf mahalanobis, 1% false-alarm threshold) with a k-consecutive alert rule; randomforest vs lda diagnosis under random and time-block splits power demand forecasting: day-ahead 24-hour forecasts from kpx 2025 national hourly demand and open-meteo temperature — features use only values at least 24 hours old (with a leakage test), holidays included; baseline, linear, gbm and ensemble tested on october–december dart data mart: opendart collection (status-code handling, rate-limit waits), standardised accounts, pivot/lag/rank sql views, and evidence search over business-report paragraphs with character-bigram bm25, returned with sources (api key only via secrets) analysis warehouse: eight questions on power demand, temperature, solar irradiance and data-job postings, each answered by dbt analysis tables — a two-segment temperature model on weekdays (breakpoints found by a 0.5 °c grid search), day types re-classified with a holiday seed to compare days off and long holidays, peak hour by season, the spring midday dip and a test of its cause (a month-fixed-effect regression gives −2,704 mw of midday demand per 100 w/m² of irradiance, while the 20:00–23:00 placebo shows +11 mw, i.e. no effect — consistent with unmetered solar), and skill mentions by data role. sources are modelled in dbt (duckdb) as staging → intermediate → marts → analysis, with the hour's start time as key so '24:00' never slips into the next day · the airflow dag, cli and tests share the same functions power-transition analysis: ember monthly generation and our world in data energy data (keyless open data) analysed with seven sql queries — korea's 25-year electricity mix, coal decline vs 11 other countries, solar growth and seasonality, carbon intensity — published as a d3 dashboard with an animated year scatter; coal 46.3% (2009) → 31.1% (2025), solar share peaks in may (7.6%) vs december (3.4%), the same direction as the warehouse's spring midday dip api monitoring (api watch): checks 22 public apis on a regular schedule — beyond http 200 it flags stale data, empty results, duplicates and type changes, stores the first healthy schema to tell added fields from removed or retyped ones, and groups repeated failures into one issue (includes a django admin and docker compose version) wildfire risk map: compares the fosberg fire weather index with nasa satellite fire detections daily — most detections are persistent heat sources such as steelworks, so rules filter them out data agent: an mcp server that lets an llm query these results in sql — read-only sql guards and a check that numbers in the answer match the query results power demand: mape 6.17% for the same-hour-last-week baseline → 3.23% for the ensemble; daily-peak error 2.64% sensor diagnosis: randomforest scored 0.99+ on every component with a random split but 0.81 ± 0.10 on the valve under 5-fold time-series cv; lda held 0.99 ± 0.02 (valve) and 1.00 (pump) across test windows, while the accumulator (0.47) remains open earthquakes: b = 1.11 ± 0.05 on 2,474 events of m4+ in east asia (the catalogue updates daily) · 39 tests across the four projects analysis: above 17.5 °c weekday demand rises +1,636 mw per °c, below 13 °c +969 mw (r² 0.83); saturdays −10.8% and sundays/holidays −16.7% vs weekdays; lunar new year and chuseok −21.6% and −18.7% vs nearby weekdays; on 14 of 22 april weekdays midday demand fell below the night minimum · data-engineer postings mention sql 90% and spark 68%, data-analyst postings sql 51% and tableau 27% (107 postings over one week, so no trend claims yet) warehouse: 44 models (12 analysis tables) · 129 dbt tests · 42 pytest cases; the analysis dashboard is recomputed daily · airflow verified for a single dag run only (not operated continuously) api monitoring: success rate is reported only as the share of observed checks (not called uptime), and the rules are covered by 34 tests — about 130 pytest tests across the eight projects python sql dbt duckdb airflow docker scikit-learn github actions time series

t: Data-driven portfolio generator — YAML → Korean/English site · resume PDFs · automated checks
s: data-driven portfolio generator — yaml → korean/english site · resume pdfs · automated checks a static-site generator that keeps portfolio content as yaml data; the build produces korean/english pages, project pages, resume pdfs and a search index, and deploys only after automated checks pass the same experiences were written separately in resumes (1-page, full, role-specific, english), the web portfolio, notion and linkedin, so figures and wording drifted and every fix had to be made in several places keep facts in one place, generate everything else from it, and let the machine catch broken pages before deployment data: activities and projects stored in star form in data/portfolio.yaml (korean) and portfolio.en.yaml (english); per-project design decisions and retrospectives in case_notes.yaml build: python + jinja2 generate the main page, 14 project pages (ko/en), resumes (1-page, full, data/ai role, english) with 5 pdfs printed by playwright, a search index, share images, sitemap and notion/linkedin text in one run checks: missing fields and links fail the build under --strict; link checks on every page and desktop/phone layout checks (overflow, overlap) run before deploy private material: contact details, evidence and interview answers are committed only as files sealed with a public key (rsa-oaep + aes-gcm); github actions unseals them with a secret key and emits encrypted pages only — no plaintext in the repository extras: 'ask my portfolio' (site passages with sources, no llm), a rag citation-check mini demo, a career map of studied regions (natural earth) and an ai-trend post series one edit updates the korean/english site, resume pdfs and project pages together, so an error such as an award's english name is fixed everywhere at once every deploy must pass link checks on all pages (90+) and desktop/phone layout checks python jinja2 yaml github actions playwright javascript

t: Encrypted study notes & interview-prep apps — a PBKDF2 · AES-GCM PWA on static hosting
s: encrypted study notes & interview-prep apps — a pbkdf2 · aes-gcm pwa on static hosting study and interview-practice apps whose content is encrypted at build time, hosted as a static site and decrypted in the browser with a password ssafy lecture notes, interview answers and cover letters cannot go into a public repository, yet i needed to review and practise on my phone while on the move — without running a server deploy the content encrypted using only static hosting (github pages), so that only someone with the password can open it in the browser encryption: at build time each page is sealed with aes-gcm under a key derived by pbkdf2-sha256 (600k iterations) and decrypted with the browser's web crypto; one key per build, so a single unlock per tab opens both apps. builds without a password emit empty lock pages only study app: titles, outlines and summaries extracted from 57 notes; 1,656 practice questions (multiple choice, cloze, written), keyword cards, weakness report and mock exams; the full-text index is gzipped and encrypted with the same key; spaced review at 1·3·7·14·30 days interview app: question bank with typical vs strong answers, answer skeletons and decks generated from portfolio data (presenter mode; pdf/pptx built in the unlocked browser), timed/recorded mock interviews, an opic practice set, recruiting info for 38 organisations, 30 cover-letter prompts with core-experience balancing, goal d-days and weekly checks operation: the scheduled job adds new questions as public-key-sealed add-on files without the private key and the deploy build merges them; math fonts moved to one shared file to cut note size by more than half; progress moves between devices as password-protected files that merge rather than overwrite runs on github pages with no server and leaves no plaintext in the repository or the deployment · moving math fonts to a shared file cut encrypted notes from about 44 mb to 20 mb bottom tab bar on phones and offline install (pwa); main desktop and phone flows pass automated checks javascript web crypto pwa python cryptography playwright

t: Hankki — a fridge-inventory meal and workout coach agent (LangGraph · FastAPI · Android)
s: hankki — a fridge-inventory meal and workout coach agent (langgraph · fastapi · android) a korean web and android app that works out menus, missing ingredients and the time left after cooking from fridge stock (weight and use-by date), and turns one sentence about your situation into a recommendation, a shopping list and a cooking mode having tofu in the fridge doesn't tell you whether it's enough for two, whether it must be used this week, or whether there's time to work out after cooking. in ssafy ai core project 3 (solo) i built the agent at the centre of this, and i'm extending it into the final project. solo, from planning and design (use cases, system, erd) to the agent, fastapi backend, web ui and android shell. goal: even when the model is wrong, numbers like stock and portions must not be. agent flow: langgraph analyse (model: natural language → conditions) → plan (rules fix the core tasks; the model only picks helper tools from the tool list via a structured plan output) → execute (worker) → judge (stock, use-by date, missing grams, cooking time — in code) ⟲ replan (max 3) → verify → respond (sentences from confirmed values only) safeguards: unregistered tools and duplicate tasks are dropped in code; if the model call fails the rule plan carries on alone · a missing provider key is reported as missing_key with a direct search link · keys and raw exceptions never reach user replies or run logs task chaining: 'i want kimchi stew — what do i need to buy?' → recipe lookup → compare with fridge stock → pass only the missing ingredients to shopping search. 'two of us, only what we have' applies servings and leaves the cart alone · every action is shown with an undo button run records: event bus → logging agent (no llm) → sqlite subscription stores analyse/plan/execute/judge/respond with tool arguments, latency and replan reasons, and flags duplicate calls, off-plan calls, repeated failures of one tool and the replan cap — logging errors never block the conversation grounded answers (rag): 31 guide documents summarising public sources (nutrient intake standards, food safety, exercise guidelines, with source links) indexed in chroma; questions no api can answer get evidence paragraphs and sources, or 'not found' when nothing relevant exists domain: 110 hand-written single-serving recipes (calories and protein from usda references), package-level stock with use-by dates, a cooking mode that recomputes missing grams when servings change, skill-level workout routines with set timers, schedule-overlap checks and back-calculated cooking start times fixed defects: re-sending after a lost response could double water/intake records → the first request id is reused so the server total rises once · beef stayed in plant-based candidates → ingredient categories were tightened and external recipes whose ingredients can't be verified are excluded from automatic candidates ui and delivery: web with mobile bottom tabs and a desktop sidebar, android webview shell (notifications, health connect daily totals preview), debug apk and unsigned aab builds, per-browser data isolation checked in the docker production image tests: pytest with a stand-in model (fake llm) and fixed provider responses, so it runs without keys; run on github actions six representative scenarios (enough ingredients, candidate replan, replan cap, missing provider key, no tool needed, time limit) match expected values, tool-call counts and replan counts 110 automated tests passing, 4 real-account checks run on demand (final submission re-run 2026-11-20) · ingredient entry → cooking → intake → records exercised by hand in mobile 390×844 and desktop 1440×940 browsers still to verify: the full path with real model, food-safety and youtube keys; health connect permission revocation and notifications on a real android device; account-level storage python langgraph langchain fastapi pydantic sqlite chromadb android pytest

t: POSPEAK (KILL KONG) — Konglish → natural English correction AI (FLAN-T5 · Qwen + RAG)
s: pospeak (kill kong) — konglish → natural english correction ai (flan-t5 · qwen + rag) a generator plus retrieval (rag) that rewrites awkward or konglish sentences into natural english konglish and stiff formal english slip past grammar checkers; learners need natural, context-aware rewrites build the correction data and find a training strategy for t5-family models [own] built and cleaned word-level and context-level correction pairs [own] fine-tuned flan-t5 with lora and compared three strategies (word→context, context→word, joint) with bertscore [final service kill kong — the final version of pospeak] qwen-2.5 (1.5b) fine-tuned on 2,000 conversational lines from friends + a 630-entry konglish rag db + per-user memory (mistake notes), combined with langchain in a react native · fastapi mobile app [team] rag pipeline and cli that retrieve the top-5 similar correction examples with multilingual sentence embeddings (paraphrase-multilingual-minilm) and faiss and feed them to the model found catastrophic forgetting in sequential training (bertscore f1 0.47 → 0.32) and switched to joint training the jointly trained model reached a validation bertscore f1 of about 0.74 (vs 0.32–0.47 for sequential training) team project encouragement award python hugging face flan-t5 lora rag faiss

t: Wavenumber correlation of gravity & magnetic data for salt/basement structure (M.S. · SPE Journal first author)
s: wavenumber correlation of gravity & magnetic data for salt/basement structure (m.s. · spe journal first author) separated overlapping gravity and magnetic signals in the wavenumber domain to resolve salt and basement structures offshore abu dhabi in the ghasha field offshore abu dhabi, salt and basement lie under 8–10 km of sediments, so gravity and magnetic signals overlap; earlier methods put the salt at ~6,000 m, far shallower than the ~9,300 m seen in seismic data propose an analysis that separates basement and salt signals in airborne gravity and magnetic data built a wavenumber correlation filtering (wcf) pipeline — upward continuation and normalization, then the correlation coefficient cc(k) between the two signals at each wavenumber designed two indices — slfi from positively correlated components (basement) and dlfi from weak/negative ones (salt) chose thresholds from energy–correlation trade-off curves instead of by eye (upward continuation 1,500 m at the knee point; slfi band 0.5–1.0 keeps ~half the energy at correlation 0.85) validated against three independent published models with map, profile and 3-d density comparisons presented abu dhabi processing and analysis results at 10+ regular lab research meetings (2024.05–2026.01) and at the 2025.11 basic research lab workshop researcher on national r&d projects, including the iitp global talent program slfi basement structure agrees with three independent models at r ≥ 0.94 (profile correlation 0.95–0.98 after shift alignment) dlfi reproduces the salt distribution and suggests an additional salt uplift west of ghasha first-author paper in spe journal (scie, 2026, with univ. of calgary and khalifa univ.) · 3 conference talks (2024) m.s. degree conferred 2026.08.21 signal processing correlation analysis index design gravity & magnetic data

t: Research stay at the University of Calgary — joint interpretation of gravity & magnetic data
s: research stay at the university of calgary — joint interpretation of gravity & magnetic data combined gravity and magnetic surveys to characterize the ghasha salt dome and basement salt domes and basement are hard to interpret from one type of survey alone carry out joint gravity–magnetic interpretation research during a ~6-month stay funded by the msit/iitp global talent program in digital fields (ai & digital-twin smart ccs) worked with the department of geomatics engineering on wavenumber correlation of airborne gravity and magnetic data extended the work into a 3-institution collaboration with khalifa university (uae) joined a field geophysical survey in kananaskis (canadian rockies) and co-wrote the english field exploration report (2024.08) the stay led to a first-author paper accepted in spe journal (scie, 2026) completed the same research as the m.s. thesis (2026) gravity & magnetic data joint interpretation international collaboration

t: Seismic interpretation of large overseas CO2 storage sites considering plate-tectonic history (first-author paper)
s: seismic interpretation of large overseas co2 storage sites considering plate-tectonic history (first-author paper) reconstructed how large overseas co2 storage sites formed and interpreted their seismic images from a structural-geology perspective korea needs ~30 mt/yr of domestic co2 storage by 2050, but there was little systematic analysis of how large storage sites form geologically as first author, compare large co2 storage sites in four regions from a plate-tectonic viewpoint (submitted 2023.07, accepted 2023.12) reconstructed the plate-tectonic history of four regions with gplates (paleomap paleoatlas) interpreted seismic images of two representative ccs projects per region — quest & weyburn-midale, northern lights & porthos, gorgon & moomba, uthmaniyah & qatar lng — focusing on reservoir and cap rock earlier studies: applicability of gpu-based 4d seismic monitoring (2022); case reviews of deep-learning seismic imaging in saudi arabia and geophysical monitoring at sleipner, norway (2023) short stay at univ. of calgary (2023.12–2024.02): processed gravity data from the utah forge geothermal site → poster at the kseg spring conference 2024 first-author paper: analysis on seismic interpretation for overseas large-scale co2 storage considering geological history related to plate tectonics, geophysics and geophysical exploration 27(1), 1–22 (2024) showed that stratigraphy in each seismic image reflects the region's tectonic history → a basis for rejecting geologically unrealistic velocity models when processing domestic data 1 second-author paper (carbonnet ccs, gippsland basin, 2023) · 3 conference talks (2022–2023) outstanding student paper award (poster), kseg spring conference 2024 — accuracy of seismic velocity and density models at the utah forge site seismic interpretation gplates plate reconstruction ccs

t: IAB capstone — Wildfire spread prediction with spatiotemporal deep learning
s: iab capstone — wildfire spread prediction with spatiotemporal deep learning a u-lstm that predicts the next wildfire front from the current front, weather and terrain wildfires spread quickly with wind and vegetation, yet korea had no real-time spread prediction model design and train the spatiotemporal model that predicts where the fire will be next input rasters: fire fronts digitized in gis from korea forest service fire maps, plus weather, ndvi and elevation designed a u-lstm (conv2d encoder → lstm → conv2dtranspose decoder) kept shallow at 2,736 parameters because data were scarce expanded the short time series with sliding windows of length 1–19 into 151 training batches implemented the model in tensorflow and pytorch and evaluated it with overall accuracy and f1-score input data: fire fronts, elevation, ndvi, wind direction and speed of four large fires (uljin–samcheok, gunwi, miryang, gangneung) rasterized in arcgis — three for training, one held out to test generalization unseen fire (gangneung): accuracy 0.90 · f1 0.85 (validation 0.95 · 0.81) refactored the team notebooks into a tested python package and documented the limitations on github python tensorflow pytorch u-lstm arcgis
